title: (Senior) Softwareentwickler (m/w/x) Testautomatisierung
description: Projektbeschreibung: Technologie begeistert Sie? Uns auch! Zur Verstärkung unseres Expertenteams bei unserem Kunden aus der Funk- und Kommunikationsbranche suchen wir einen (Senior) Softwareentwickler (m/w/x) Testautomatisierung in Festanstellung bei K-tronik. Aufgaben: Du konzipierst, entwickelst und betreibst eine zentrale Testautomatisierungsplattform für komplexe Funkkommunikationssysteme. title: Post-doctorant : « Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Renewable Energy Production and Storage in Subsurface Reservoirs”
description: Contexte : ENSTA est un établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées. L’école a pour mission la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, dont les ingénieurs de l'armement et les ingénieurs des études et techniques de l'armement, ainsi que des cadres et docteurs hautement qualifiés pour les secteurs public et privé, en particulier dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et des technologies de pointe.   ENSTA accompagne par sa recherche, son innovation et son offre de formation la transformation des grands secteurs stratégiques nationaux répondant ainsi aux enjeux de souveraineté nationale. Elle dispose de 3 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR) organisées autour de 9 laboratoires de recherche (UER) qui mènent une recherche appliquée en relation étroite avec l’industrie.   ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris) . Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID)). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans , inauguré en janvier 2025. Des chercheurs de l’école travaillent également en collaboration dans le cadre d'études portées par les centres Hi-Paris, lauréat en 2024 IA Cluster, E4C ou E4H notamment. ENSTA résulte de la fusion le 1er janvier 2025 d’ENSTA Paris et d’ENSTA Bretagne.  Son siège est situé à Palaiseau (91), sur le campus de Paris-Saclay et elle a un autre campus à Brest. Elle met en place une nouvelle formation d’ingénieur unifiée sur les deux campus (Paris-Saclay et Brest) à la rentrée académique 2026/2027.   Rejoindre l'école, c'est intégrer un établissement engagé pour la parité et l'égalité professionnelle, la diversité et l'accompagnement de ses agents en situation de handicap , dès le recrutement et tout au long de la carrière. Afin de préserver le bien-être au travail, l'école mène une politique active en matière de conditions de travail, reposant notamment sur un juste équilibre entre vie personnelle et vie professionnelle.   Sujet : « Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Renewable Energy Production and Storage in Subsurface Reservoirs” Ce poste fait partie de la subvention « Leveraging AI for Sustainable Renewable Energy Production and Storage », financée par Hi ! Paris (https://www.hi-paris.fr/). La recherche sera menée à l'ENSTA, Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Le poste offre l'opportunité de travailler sur un sujet de recherche stimulant et impactant. Les connaissances, l'innovation et les compétences développées dans le cadre de ce poste offriront d'excellentes perspectives d'évolution de carrière tant dans l'industrie que dans le monde universitaire. Le changement climatique exige des stratégies innovantes pour exploiter les énergies renouvelables. Le sous-sol de la Terre offre un potentiel important grâce à des technologies telles que l'énergie géothermique profonde, le stockage souterrain de l'hydrogène et le captage, l'utilisation et le stockage du carbone (CCUS). Ces méthodes pourraient transformer le paysage énergétique de la France et de l'Europe, mais elles sont souvent entravées par la sismicité induite par l'injection de fluides dans la croûte terrestre. Pour relever ce défi, il faut des solutions avancées. La théorie du contrôle mathématique, telle qu'explorée dans le projet INJECT du CER (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101087771), offre des stratégies pour minimiser les risques sismiques tout en optimisant la production d'énergie. title: Principal of backend
description: About SchemeServe SchemeServe is insurance software like no other. Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support. Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values. We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats. We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it. We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post. We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work. If you're excited, good! So are we. Come and join the Insurtech revolution! Principal Backend Engineer UK Remote We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better. You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction. But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design. Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software. You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement. What We Mean By Principal This is a deeply technical role. You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers. But technical knowledge alone isn't enough. We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software. Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments. We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us. That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs. Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology. Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have. Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution. We're quite comfortable with that. How You'll Lead Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority . We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with: "We'd better ask the Principal Engineer." If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own. Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience. And be prepared to change your own mind too. The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one. Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you. You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team. But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded . The Technical Challenge Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years. At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services. Our backend estate includes: .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET. TypeScript services. Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis. Azure cloud infras

title: Senior Systems Engineer - Autonomy Behavior
description: Description Senior Systems Engineer - Autonomy Behavior The Role As a Senior Autonomy Behavior Systems Engineer, you will help define and validate how an autonomous vehicle behaves in the real world. You will own one or more behavior areas from requirements through simulation evaluation, road-data review, and release recommendation. This role sits at the intersection of systems engineering, software validation, simulation, and safety. You will turn broad product and safety goals into clear behavior definitions, testable requirements, metrics, test plans, and evidence. You will also need to understand what the results mean, where they are weak, and what should happen next. What You'll Do Own end-to-end validation for one or more autonomous driving behaviors, from initial behavior scoping and requirements definition to product launch. Combine simulation, road data, closed-course testing, and expert review to evaluate behavior across large scenario sets, diverse conditions, software versions, and fleet configurations. Define, deploy, and refine metrics, test strategies and acceptance criteria for autonomous behavior for simulation and road. Partner with teams across and outside the autonomy organization to assess, author, and present behavior readiness for release and launch decisions. Required Qualifications Master's degree in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related field. 5 or more years of professional experience in systems engineering, autonomous vehicles, robotics, simulation, or safety-critical validation. Proven experience evaluating autonomous vehicles in support of a self-driving fleet launch. Strong understanding of systems engineering fundamentals, including system decomposition, use-case definition, requirements authoring, interface definition, verification planning, and traceability. Professional experience designing or executing simulation-based evaluations at scale, not just isolated scenario demonstrations. Strong Python experience for data analysis, test automation, simulation workflows, and engineering tools and exposure to agentic workflows. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of working effectively across teams. Demonstrated ability to manage stakeholders, resolve ambiguity, set expectations, and drive work to completion without waiting for a perfect process. What Will Give You a Competitive Edge Experience with human benchmarking for behavioral or safety evaluation, including attentive human benchmark data, human percentiles, or expert labeling. Experience with counterfactual analysis in simulation, including comparing an autonomous vehicle response with a human or alternate-system response under the same scene conditions. Familiarity with safety cases, safety claims, and the role of validation evidence in supporting them. Experience with hazard analysis, including structured hazard analysis, scenario-based hazard analysis, failure analysis, or similar methods. Understanding of risk quantification, risk acceptance, risk budgets, and mitigation prioritization. Experience translating legal or regulatory expectations into behavioral requirements, metrics, test coverage, or compliance evidence. Experience with large scenario libraries, synthetic test generation, replay-to-simulation workflows, simulation test protocols, or validation scorecards.
